metadata.technology_reasoning: Roller compactors are widely used in pharmaceutical and chemical industries for dry granulation processes. They consist of rollers that compress powder into sheets, which are then milled. This configuration is the industry standard due to its efficiency and scalability in producing granules without moisture or heat.

components.reasoning: Core functional components applying pressure to powder for densification. They are separate, precision-manufactured units essential to the compaction process.
Delivers powder uniformly to the rollers. Usually a distinct subsystem, critical for consistent granulation quality.
Remove compacted ribbons from rollers to prevent buildup; typically procured or manufactured separately.
Provides mechanical power to rotate rollers and feeders. Separate assembly from the rollers, standardized across designs.
Controls operational parameters such as roller speed and pressure; modular unit with distinct supplier chains.
Mills compacted ribbons into granules; often a separate component integrated downstream but critical to the process.
Provides mechanical support and alignment for all components; procured as a major assembly or fabricated structure.

Compaction Rollers.name: Steel Ingots
Compaction Rollers.reasoning: Primary structural material providing high strength and durability, essential for manufacturing rollers that withstand heavy compaction loads; steel ingots are the base material before forming.

Compaction Rollers.name: Carbon
Compaction Rollers.reasoning: Carbon is a key element in steel alloys, contributing to hardness and strength of the rollers; universally present in all steel used in compaction rollers.

Compaction Rollers.name: Titanium
Compaction Rollers.reasoning: Sometimes used as alloying element or coating to improve wear resistance and strength, but alternatives like hardened steel often suffice, hence moderate confidence.

Compaction Rollers.name: Aluminum
Compaction Rollers.reasoning: Used occasionally for lightweight rollers or components but less common than steel, so uncertain but possible.

Feeding System (Powder Feeder).name: Aluminum
Feeding System (Powder Feeder).reasoning: Commonly used in feeder housing and components for lightweight and corrosion resistance, industry standard though some alternatives exist.

Feeding System (Powder Feeder).name: Stainless steel (SS 304/316)
Feeding System (Powder Feeder).reasoning: Critical for components contacting powders due to corrosion resistance and hygiene, universally used in powder feeders.

Feeding System (Powder Feeder).name: Polyethylene
Feeding System (Powder Feeder).reasoning: Used for wear-resistant liners or parts in direct contact with powder; commonly used but polymer alternatives exist.

Feeding System (Powder Feeder).name: Copper
Feeding System (Powder Feeder).reasoning: Used in electrical parts within feeder motors and sensors; moderately confident due to presence of alternatives like aluminum wiring.

Scraper Blades.name: Tool steel

Scraper Blades.name: Carbon

Scraper Blades.name: Titanium carbide

Scraper Blades.name: Polyethylene
Scraper Blades.reasoning: Used in some scraper blade edges for flexible scraping or covers but not universal, thus uncertain.

Drive System (Motor and Gearbox).name: Titanium

Drive System (Motor and Gearbox).name: Polyethylene
